Same $10,000 grows to $150K, or $76K. The difference is a 10-year-later start.
$10,000 at an example 7% a year grows to $149,745 in 40 years, but $76,123 in 30.
About half the 40-year pile arrives in the last 10 years.
US stocks returned about 10% a year from 1928 through 2025, roughly 7% after inflation. Past returns aren't a promise.
Cards charging interest averaged 22.15% in Q2 2026: compounding works on debt too.
Sources: NYU Stern (Damodaran) historical returns; Federal Reserve G.19.
News and education, not financial advice.
